title: Half lantern
description: Split one pair twist in the puncture-capped lantern, use two Hurwitz moves, and combine the neighboring pair twists into a square. The one-boundary correction is derived, but framed equality is not yet engine-checked.

sections.Surface and conventions: A disk with three marked points. The relation is exact after capping any proposed inner boundaries to punctures.
sections.Derivation: T123 = T12 T13 T23 = H12 (T23 H12 T23^-1) T23^2, via splitting, two Hurwitz moves, and combining.
sections.Braid factorization: (sigma1 sigma2)^3 = sigma1 (sigma2^2 sigma1 sigma2^-2) sigma2^4 in the project convention; the complete Artin action verifies it.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: The playground draws both half-twist arcs and the squared closed-curve twist using the shared surface library.
sections.Standard mapping classes: One twist enclosing three punctures becomes two positive half twists and a squared positive pair twist.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: The checked direct substitution matches the existing five-step interactive Hurwitz walkthrough and transports through an outer conjugator.
sections.References: See the linked derivation and Margalit–McCammond, Theorem 5.1, on replacing punctures with inner boundaries.
